judgment.reason: The query follows by classical logical derivation from premises p22 and p3. Given an arbitrary person x: (1) by p22, there exists a person y such that x admires y—call this witness c; (2) by p3, if x admires c, then c helps x; (3) therefore c helps x; (4) therefore there exists a person y such that y helps x; (5) since x was arbitrary, this holds for every person. The logical chain is valid. The False side's objections rely on closed-world assumptions ('helping facts must be stated, not derived'), which contradicts the instruction to use classical logic without closed-world assumptions. The 28 register premises are orthogonal to the admiration-helping chain and do not undermine it. The witness provided by p22 is explicitly a person in the domain, so instantiation into p3 is licensed. Self-help (when x = y) is not excluded and still satisfies the query.
